metadata.title: Infrastructure reliability incident investigation
metadata.artifact_scope_note: Evidence is aggregated query output (not raw log lines or metric samples); it contains no chat/communication records.

incident_description: Reliability incident investigation of a production environment. Evidence consists of Elasticsearch aggregation results over application and proxy logs, Kubernetes, cloud-provider and host system events, Prometheus Alertmanager alerts, change-management / CI-CD audit records and metric anomaly detection. No root cause, impact or trigger is stated; these must be established from the supplied artifacts. Environment context: Organization: Meridian Utilities (electricity retailer, customers billed in US Central time); Platform: on-premises Kubernetes cluster mu-prod, node range 10.33.0.0/16; Billing: the daily autopay charge run is a Kubernetes CronJob (default/autopay-charge-run, schedule '30 1 * * *', timeZone America/Chicago) that submits card charges through card-processor-gw; a ledger-reconciler compares payments to invoices hourly; Change management: CHG- identifiers; CronJob executions are recorded by Job name.
investigation_questions: Which automation run produced the duplicate charges? Provide its identifier.
Which account or automation identity executed the triggering change?
Which external payment processor endpoint received the duplicate charge requests?
During what hour did the first signs of the failure appear? Provide the earliest date and time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC format.

What is the root cause category of the incident: configuration change, software defect, hardware failure, cloud provider failure, capacity exhaustion, automation error, certificate expiry, or third-party dependency failure?
What scheduling condition caused the job to run twice for the same local billing date?
Which of the three CIA components is primarily affected: availability, integrity, or confidentiality?
According to the error volume statistics, what single service emitted the most errors? Is it the root cause or a downstream symptom?
Which change restored normal service? Provide its change identifier.
